Demonstrations may show that the output fills the whole grid with a periodic color sequence indexed by that invariant. Use zero-based row/column coordinates and verify the sign convention against observed output: for down-right stripes, `column−row` indexes the phase; for down-left stripes, `row+column` does. Infer the smallest plausible period and color per phase by checking which candidate periods avoid assigning different colors to the same residue; use demo output to establish the complete mapping when available. Then color every cell from its phase, rather than preserving only the sparse markers. Verify several cells against each demonstrated line and ensure the resulting output reproduces every demo. Do not assume the marker positions alone give every residue's color; use output examples to establish the complete mapping.
6. When demonstrations show color 1 marking an absent continuation at a grid edge, compare repeated rows, bands, or motif copies to infer the expected continuation and affected cells. It may be a solid suffix or only selected motif-phase positions. Color only the confirmed missing continuation cells; preserve the existing motif and unrelated cells. Check the candidate against every demo's changed and unchanged cells, and select repeated copies from that evidence—not from rightmost zeros or suffix length alone.
7. Choose exactly one legal action. Request a demonstration only when its expected information is worth its cost; submit when the rule is adequately supported; finish only after the instance is over. Account for the stated scoring penalties and caps.
